messages.author: a995fce295e7d803
messages.subject: distsamp vs. DISTANCE with hierarchical sampling design
parts:
Hi all,

I'm a relatively new to unmarked, so please forgive my likely
clumsiness. I'm attempting to use distsamp to repeat some previously
conducted analyses from DISTANCE and running into some trouble.

The data are structured as follows: point counts were conducted at 36
sites with multiple points within each site. Points were visited
multiple times over the course of a summer.

I am able to get unmarked and DISTANCE to agree (exactly) under the
following conditions:
1. I use a site- and visit-specific (site and visit seem to define a
"stratum" in Distance) detection function and density estimate in
DISTANCE.
2. I narrow the dataset in R to include only a single visit to a
single site and use a null model in distsamp.
3. As a result the density and the parameters of the detection
function for the visit and site modeled in unmarked will match those
from DISTANCE.

I have been unable to make any headway at replicating the results at
higher levels of the sample hierarchy, despite trying to use distsamp
on all visits to a single site with Visit as a covariate and to the
entire data set. I recognize this issue has come up before, but it
didn't seem to come to any concrete resolution in terms of how to go
about specifying the model to make them reproducible across programs.

Thanks for any guidance!
Joshua Goldberg

parts:
hi Joshua,
 Do you mean that you cant get the same result with DISTANCE and unmarked?
 Note: DISTANCE is not fitting the same model so there's no reason to expect the result to be the same.
 If you mean that you can't get unmarked's function(s) to produce an estimate for the replicated case, then send me your data set and R script and I'll look at it.
regards
andy

parts:
Hi Richard,

I came across this post while looking for some explanation of why my predicted estimates using gdistsamp() are so unreasonable, and I saw your reply to this post. In my case I visited all my sites 3 times, so my plan was to just use them as extra effort, but while reading through the discussions in the forum I decided that gdistsamp was the best function for my analysis, and the covariates seemed to make sense, but I hit a wall when I got to the predictions. This is the link to my previous post:
https://mail.google.com/mail/u/0/#search/unmarked/15df3f9db05afa1a

Do you think I should actually be using distsamp()? I've actually ran the models with distsamp, and I do get reasonable predictions and CI, but the only covariate that comes up as affecting abundance is the one that was actually affecting availability in gdistsamp(). Am I missing something on how to interpret those predictions? 

I really appreciate If you or others in the group could shed some light on this. 

Thank you,

Fernanda.
